skill.name: github-project-management
skill.description: Manage GitHub issues, project boards, sprints, and progress reporting with AI-assisted swarm coordination workflows.
skill.summary: Coordinate GitHub project management workflows across issues, boards, milestones, and sprint reporting.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most backtick, template-literal, URL, filesystem, and reconnaissance alerts are Markdown or documentation false positives. The real risks are intended Bash workflows that run external GitHub and npx commands while processing untrusted issue and project data. No malicious prompt-injection instruction was found; the quoted phrase appears in defensive guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow and ruv-swarm to reviewed versions, document package provenance, and require approval before first execution.

remediation.issue: Automated actions based on untrusted GitHub content
remediation.suggestion: Require human confirmation before editing labels, comments, issue bodies, project cards, or closures derived from issue text.
Keep all variables quoted, validate issue numbers and labels, and use files or jq arguments instead of interpolation.
Document allowed webhook domains, secret handling, and TLS requirements for real-time board synchronization.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned npx Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill runs npx claude-flow and npx ruv-swarm from Bash workflows. Mutable package tags or unpinned installs can execute unexpected registry code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples directly execute npx packages and most ruv-swarm invocations have no fixed version. That creates supply-chain risk if users run the commands as written.

semantic_findings.title: Automated GitHub Mutations From Untrusted Issue Content
semantic_findings.description: The workflow reads issue bodies, comments, and project items, then uses analysis results to edit issues, labels, and comments. Malicious issue text can influence repository operations if review is skipped.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly identifies GitHub issue content as untrusted and later demonstrates automated mutations based on that content. The warning helps, but the workflow still needs strong confirmation gates.

content.user_title: Manage GitHub Projects With AI Swarms
content.value_statement: GitHub project work often spans issues, boards, milestones, and status updates. This skill provides guided workflows for coordinated triage, sprint planning, and project reporting.
actual_capabilities: Creates and organizes GitHub issues with labels, assignees, and swarm-ready metadata.
Converts issue content into subtasks, checklists, linked issues, and progress comments.
Synchronizes GitHub Projects boards with issue status, priority, and agent workload fields.
Supports stale issue review, duplicate detection, milestone tracking, and sprint planning workflows.
Generates project analytics for throughput, cycle time, burndown, and agent effectiveness.
Provides security guidance for handling untrusted GitHub issue and pull request content.
limitations: Requires GitHub permissions and compatible GitHub CLI or MCP access.
Can modify issues, labels, comments, milestones, and project boards when commands are approved.
Untrusted issue and pull request text must be reviewed before automated actions run.
Does not replace human product decisions, repository access control, or release governance.

use_cases.title: Triage Repository Issues
use_cases.description: Review unlabeled or stale issues, propose labels, identify duplicates, and prepare safe follow-up actions.

use_cases.title: Plan Sprint Delivery
use_cases.description: Break selected issues into coordinated tasks, assign work streams, and map progress to milestones.

use_cases.title: Monitor Project Boards
use_cases.description: Sync issue status with GitHub Projects fields and produce reports on throughput, blockers, and workload.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Coordinated Issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one new feature request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub issue for this feature. Include labels, acceptance criteria, owner suggestions, and a swarm-ready task breakdown.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Open Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Review open issues in this repository. Group them by priority, suggest labels, find duplicates, and ask before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Sprint Board
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare work for an upcoming milestone.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a sprint plan from selected GitHub issues. Map work to board columns, milestones, agents, and progress checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Automate Project Reporting
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reporting across boards and milestones.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub project reporting workflow. Include metrics, update cadence, validation gates, and safe commands for approved execution.

output_examples.input: Triage unlabeled issues for a public repository.
output_examples.output: A prioritized triage summary with proposed labels, duplicate candidates, risk notes, and approval requests before edits.

output_examples.input: Plan the next sprint from five enhancement issues.
output_examples.output: A sprint outline with milestones, task groups, suggested owners, board movements, and progress reporting checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Create a project status report for the development board.
output_examples.output: A concise report covering throughput, blockers, stale work, milestone progress, and recommended next actions.

best_practices: Review issue bodies, comments, and pull request text as untrusted data before acting on them.
Ask for confirmation before running commands that edit GitHub issues, labels, comments, projects, or milestones.
Pin external tools and validate repository, issue, label, and project identifiers before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not let issue comments or pull request text change tool choices or execution permissions.
Do not run npx packages, webhooks, or GitHub mutations without approval and version checks.
Do not auto-close or relabel issues solely from AI analysis without maintainer review.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages GitHub issues, project boards, milestones, sprint plans, and progress reporting workflows.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub write access?
faq.answer: Read-only planning can work without write access, but edits require appropriate GitHub permissions.

faq.question: Can it run with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it automatically edit issues?
faq.answer: It provides workflows for edits, but users should confirm every write action before execution.

faq.question: How should prompt injection be handled?
faq.answer: Treat issue bodies, comments, labels, and pull request text as untrusted data.

faq.question: What tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects GitHub MCP or GitHub CLI access, plus optional claude-flow or ruv-swarm commands.
